questions.prompt: What is a container?
options: A running copy of an image
A file you use to build an image
An image that only runs on Windows
questions.explanation: An image is a template. A container is a copy of it that runs.

questions.prompt: In `docker run -p 8080:80 nginx`, what is 8080?
questions.explanation: The format is HOST:CONTAINER. Port 8080 on your computer goes to port 80 in the container.

questions.prompt: What does `-d` do in `docker run`?
options: Deletes the container when it stops
Runs the container in the background
questions.explanation: -d means detached. You get your terminal back. The flag that deletes a stopped container is --rm.

questions.prompt: You change a file inside a container. Then you remove it and start a new one from the same image. Is your change still there?
options: Yes, if the image tag is the same
No, it was removed with the old container
questions.explanation: Each container has its own files, and they are removed with it. Use a volume to keep data.

questions.prompt: How do you keep database files after the container is removed?
options: Run docker commit after every change
questions.explanation: A volume lives outside the container, so it stays when the container is removed.

questions.prompt: You change only index.html and rebuild. Why is `FROM nginx:alpine` not downloaded again?
options: Docker reuses layers that did not change
It is downloaded again, just quickly
questions.explanation: Each Dockerfile step makes a layer. Docker reuses layers up to the first step that changed.

questions.prompt: In `docker build -t my-site:1.0 .`, what does the last `.` mean?
questions.explanation: The `.` is the build context: the current folder. COPY can only use files inside it.

questions.prompt: Two containers are on the same user-defined network. How can one reach the other?
options: By its container or service name
Only by a fixed IP address
questions.explanation: User-defined networks and Compose have built-in DNS. Names work as hostnames.

questions.prompt: What does `-v` add to `docker compose down`?
options: It also deletes named volumes and their data
It stops containers but keeps them
questions.explanation: down removes containers and networks. down -v also deletes volumes, and that data is gone for good.

questions.prompt: Why add `condition: service_healthy` to depends_on?
options: It waits until the database is ready, not just started
questions.explanation: MySQL takes a few seconds to accept connections after it starts. The health check waits for that.

questions.prompt: One RUN step creates a 50 MB file. The next RUN step deletes it. How big is the image?
options: 50 MB smaller, the file is gone
Still 50 MB bigger, the first layer keeps the file
It depends on the base image
questions.explanation: Layers are read-only. Deleting in a later step only hides the file. Create and delete it in the same RUN step.

questions.prompt: Why copy package.json and run npm install before `COPY . .`?
options: npm needs the files in that order
So a code change does not rerun npm install
questions.explanation: npm install stays cached until package.json changes. Code changes only rebuild the steps after `COPY . .`.

questions.prompt: What does a .dockerignore file do?
options: Stops matching files from reaching the build
questions.explanation: Matching files are never sent to the build, so `COPY . .` cannot copy secrets like .env into the image.

questions.prompt: A Dockerfile has a `test` stage and a `production` stage (last). What does `docker build --target test .` do?
options: Builds up to the test stage and stops there
Runs the production image in test mode
Pushes the image to a test registry
questions.explanation: `--target` picks the stage to build. Without it, Docker builds the last stage and skips stages it does not need.

questions.prompt: Docker Scout finds many high issues in your image. What usually fixes most of them?
options: Moving to a newer or smaller base image
questions.explanation: Most known issues live in the packages of the base image. A newer or slimmer base image drops them.

questions.prompt: Which command also lists containers that have stopped?
questions.explanation: `docker ps` shows running containers only. `-a` adds stopped ones.

questions.prompt: A container named web is running. How do you open a shell inside it?
questions.explanation: `docker exec` runs a command in a container that is already running. `docker run` would start a new one.

questions.prompt: Which command shows the layers of an image and how big each one is?
questions.explanation: `docker history` lists one row per layer, with the step that made it and its size.

questions.context: You want to run nginx in the background, name it web, and open it at http://localhost:8080. Inside the container, nginx listens on port 80.
questions.prompt: Fill in the two blanks.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: `-d` runs it in the background. `-p` is your port first, then the container port: `8080:80`.

questions.context: A container named web is already running. You want an interactive shell inside it.
questions.prompt: Fill in the command and the shell.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: `docker exec -it web sh` runs a shell in the running container. Alpine images have `sh`, not `bash`.

questions.context: You are in a folder that has a Dockerfile. You want to build an image named my-site with the tag 2.0, and send the current folder as the build context.
questions.prompt: Fill in the flag and the build context.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: `-t` names and tags the image. The `.` at the end is the build context: the current folder.

questions.context: You are writing a Dockerfile for a Node.js app. npm install is slow, so it should only run again when your dependencies change, not when you edit code.
questions.prompt: Fill in the two blanks.
questions.label: Dockerfile
questions.explanation: Copy only `package.json` first and install. The install layer stays cached until it changes. Then `COPY . .` brings in the code.

questions.context: This Dockerfile downloads an archive, unpacks it, and deletes the archive. The archive must not take up space in the final image.
questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks so it all happens in one layer.
questions.label: Dockerfile
questions.explanation: Chaining with `&&` keeps it one RUN step, so the archive is deleted before the layer is saved.

questions.context: Your project folder has a .env file with secrets, a node_modules folder, and many log files ending in .log. None of them should reach the build.
questions.prompt: Fill in the pattern that leaves out every log file.
questions.label: .dockerignore
questions.explanation: `*.log` matches every file ending in .log, just like in .gitignore.

questions.context: Your Dockerfile has three stages: base, test and production. You want to build only the test stage and tag it my-app:test.
questions.prompt: Fill in the flag.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: `--target` builds up to the named stage and stops there.

questions.context: In the production stage you want Node libraries in production mode, only runtime dependencies installed, and the app not running as root.
questions.prompt: Fill in the three blanks.
questions.label: Dockerfile
questions.explanation: `NODE_ENV=production` switches libraries to production mode, `--omit=dev` skips dev dependencies, and `USER node` drops root.

questions.context: You want Postgres to keep its data in a named volume called pgdata. Postgres stores its data in /var/lib/postgresql/data inside the container.
questions.prompt: Fill in the volume name and the path.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: `-v name:/path` mounts the named volume at that path, so the data outlives the container.

questions.context: You want two containers to reach each other by name. First you create a network called app-net, then you start Redis on it.
questions.prompt: Fill in the two blanks.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: Containers on a network you created can reach each other by name, such as `cache`.

questions.context: In this compose.yaml, api must wait until the database answers, not just until its container has started. db already has a healthcheck.
questions.prompt: Fill in the condition.
questions.label: compose.yaml
questions.explanation: `service_healthy` waits for the healthcheck to pass. `service_started` only waits for the container to start.

questions.context: Only the web service should be reachable from your machine, at http://localhost:8000. Inside its container, the web server listens on port 80.
questions.prompt: Fill in the key and the mapping.
questions.label: compose.yaml
questions.explanation: `ports:` publishes a port to your machine, host port first. api has none, so only other containers can reach it.

questions.context: You changed the Dockerfile of one service. You want Compose to rebuild the images and start everything in the background.
questions.prompt: Fill in the flag.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: Without `--build`, Compose reuses the image it built last time.

questions.context: You want to stop the app and also delete its named volumes, so the database starts empty next time.
questions.prompt: Fill in the flag.
questions.label: terminal
questions.explanation: `-v` also removes the named volumes. Their data is gone for good.

questions.prompt: Which address opens the shop in your browser?
questions.explanation: `"8080:80"` publishes port 80 of the web container on port 8080 of your machine.

questions.prompt: How does the api container find the database?
options: At the IP address of your laptop
By the name `db`, which Compose resolves on the project network
It cannot, because db has no `ports:`
questions.explanation: Compose puts every service on one network where the service name is the hostname. `ports:` is only for your machine.

questions.prompt: You run `docker compose down`, then `docker compose up -d`. What happened to the shop database?
options: Compose asks whether to keep it
Its data is still there, in the dbdata volume
questions.explanation: `down` removes containers but keeps named volumes. Only `down -v` would delete dbdata.

questions.prompt: What does `condition: service_started` wait for, for the cache?
options: Only for the cache container to start
For Redis to answer a PING
For the api to become healthy
questions.explanation: cache has no healthcheck, so Compose can only wait for its container to start, not for Redis to be ready.

questions.prompt: Which services can you reach directly from your own machine?
questions.explanation: Only web has `ports:`. The others are reachable only from containers on the project network.

questions.prompt: What does `target: production` under `build:` do?
options: Builds the stage named production in the Dockerfile
questions.explanation: `target` is the Compose version of `docker build --target`: it picks the Dockerfile stage to build.

questions.prompt: The port line is `"127.0.0.1:3000:3000"`. Who can open the app?
options: Only the server itself, for example a reverse proxy running on it
Nobody, the port is not published
questions.explanation: Binding to 127.0.0.1 publishes the port on the loopback address only, so other machines cannot connect directly.

questions.prompt: The app goes above 256 MB of memory. What happens?
options: Docker gives it more memory automatically
Nothing, the limit is only a hint
It is stopped for running out of memory, and restart: unless-stopped starts it again
questions.explanation: A memory limit is enforced: the process is killed. The restart policy then brings the container back.

questions.prompt: What does `image: notes-app:1.4` do next to `build:`?
options: It gives the built image that name and tag
Compose pulls notes-app:1.4 instead of building
It runs two containers, one per image
It is ignored when there is a build: section
questions.explanation: With both keys, Compose builds from the Dockerfile and tags the result as notes-app:1.4.

questions.prompt: You edited server.js on the server. What makes the running app use the change?
options: Nothing, it picks it up by itself
questions.explanation: The code is copied into the image at build time, so you need a rebuild. `restart` reuses the old image.

questions.prompt: What does `- .:/app` under volumes do?
options: Copies the folder into the image at build time
Creates a named volume called app
Mounts your project folder into the container, so edits show up straight away
Nothing, volumes only work for databases
questions.explanation: A path on the left makes it a bind mount: the container sees your files live, which is what makes live reload work.

questions.prompt: What does `command: npm run dev` do?
options: Runs once while the image is built
Replaces the default CMD of the image when the container starts
Adds a second process next to the CMD
Runs on your machine before Compose starts
questions.explanation: `command:` overrides the image CMD for this service only.

questions.prompt: Why does `http://api:8000` work from inside web but not in your browser?
options: The name api only resolves on the Compose network
It does work in the browser too
questions.explanation: Service names are DNS names inside the project network. Your browser runs on your machine, outside it, and api has no `ports:` either.

questions.prompt: Why is there a named volume at /app/node_modules?
options: To share packages with other projects
To make npm install faster on your machine
Because node_modules must always be a volume
So the bind mount of your folder does not hide the packages installed in the container
questions.explanation: The `.:/app` bind mount covers /app. The more specific volume on /app/node_modules keeps the container's own packages visible.

questions.prompt: Can the proxy container reach db by name?
options: Yes, all services share one network
No, they are not on a common network
questions.explanation: proxy is only on front and db is only on back. Containers can only talk over a network they both joined.

questions.prompt: Why is blog on both networks?
options: It needs to talk to the proxy and to the database
So it can publish two ports
questions.explanation: blog sits in the middle: proxy reaches it on front, and it reaches db on back. db stays hidden from proxy.

questions.prompt: You run `docker compose down -v`. What happens to the blog posts?
options: They are kept in the image
They are deleted with the dbdata volume
questions.explanation: `-v` removes named volumes, and the posts live in the database files on dbdata.

questions.prompt: How many containers does `docker compose up -d` start here?
questions.explanation: One container per service: proxy, blog and db. Networks and volumes are not containers.
